This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 160 worked well for them.
msfcore on CMOS5L: Metal3 is the only horizontal signal layer, so at 60
the logic clumped and global routing overflowed (2,790); at 45 it spreads
over the free area (overflow 38, detailed routing clean).
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
msfcore: 20 ns (50 MHz) is the target, not yet signed off on CMOS5L: the
slow corner's worst path is SRAM read (6.7 ns clock-to-out with the slow
SRAM library) -> decode -> ALU -> register file (docs/plan.md section 1.2).
Timing repair: the resizer must see the slow corner (unset, it optimises
only for the typical corner and the slow corner is never repaired).
Unset, LibreLane 3.1.0.dev3 passes '-threads None' and OpenROAD runs on
one thread; 4 is a GitHub runner's core count.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
SRAM macro integration: two instances, one per 512-word bank, side by
side along the bottom (each 402.6 x 219.8 um), MX so their Metal2 pins
face up into the logic. The 43 tile pins are at the top left. On CMOS5L
the stripes are Metal4, the layer of the macros' supply columns, which
only stay vertical in R0 or MX. Project.ExtendPowerStripes (see
librelane_plugin_msf_pdn.py) moves the stripes crossing each macro onto
its columns, so the macros need not line up with the stripe pitch.
Macro liberty per corner: LibreLane loads every pattern that matches a
corner, so the patterns must not overlap (until 23 Oct 2026 "nom_*" and
"*" gave the slow corner the typical SRAM timing).
Custom PDN config: SRAM power pins are on Metal4, need Metal4↔TopMetal1 connection
SRAM GDS has no PR boundary layer; read full GDS instead of blackbox
SRAM macro internals trigger massive DRC in Magic; skip (KLayout DRC also skipped)
Blackbox SRAM macros during SPICE extraction for LVS, as the macros are not LVS clean
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
